patch.reasoning: The skill already warns against both weak truncations and inflated extras. The one success and the 22 strength-mismatch failures suggest that an explicit top-down procedure would help. Order the options by implication, test each extra clause of the top options separately, and stop at the first fully justified option. This guards against picking a weaker truncation and against being lured by an elaborate over-claim. A short checklist of typical inflations in existence statements (rational to regular, added fiber or orbit or codimension structure) covers the pattern seen here.

edits.target: 7. Commit once exactly one option survives (not false, not strictly weaker than another survivor, no unjustified extra clause). Do not switch to an option that merely looks more general or elaborate unless its extra content is justified.
edits.content: 8. Strength-ladder check (use for 'strongest / exact / complete' stems): order the options by logical implication (base statement, then base plus extra clause, and so on). Starting from the TOP of the ladder, test each extra clause separately against the stem's hypotheses. Stop at the first option whose every clause you can justify. If an option is the base statement minus a qualifier the construction obviously provides (e.g. invariance, the full range), it loses to the base statement. If it is the base statement plus a clause you cannot derive, it also loses. Do not equate 'strongest' with 'most clauses'.

## Existence statements: typical inflations to test separately
- Rational to regular: a map built from invariants or ratios defined on an open locus is naturally only rational, with indeterminacy. Upgrading to a regular morphism on the whole space is an over-claim unless a base-point-free argument is available.
- Added fiber or orbit structure ('every fiber is a single orbit', 'the reduced fiber is one orbit'): quotient-type maps usually have fibers that contain several orbits, including non-closed or degenerate ones. Check orbit and dimension counts before accepting.
- Added codimension or support clauses about the polar or bad locus ('the preimage of infinity has codimension at least 2'): a rational map to a curve has its pole locus as a divisor wherever the invariant degenerates, for example on the discriminant locus. Codimension at least 2 is suspicious.
- Dropped symmetry or invariance qualifier: an option that omits the group-invariance clause is a truncated version of the natural statement, not the strongest valid one. Prefer the option that keeps the symmetry and adds no unjustified structure.
